title: Longest Unique Substring
statement:
Find the length of the longest run of consecutive characters in which no character appears twice.

Contract
- `text` is non-null and may be empty. It may contain any `char` values, including spaces, punctuation, and non-ASCII characters; uppercase and lowercase differ.
- The run must be contiguous (a substring, not a subsequence).
- Return `0` for empty text.

Examples
- `longestUniqueLength("abacdbe")` returns `5` (the run `acdbe`).
- `longestUniqueLength("")` returns `0`.
- `longestUniqueLength("zzzz")` returns `1`.
hints: Checking every substring for repeats is far too slow. Consider a window [start, i] that is always free of repeats and ask what happens when a new character arrives.
Remember where each character was last seen. When the new character was seen inside the window, move the start just past that earlier position.

Never move the start backward: an old sighting left of the window must be ignored. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space (the table size depends on the character set, not the text), where n is the text length.
inputSyntax: Input: the text in single quotes, for example: 'abacdbe'
